TEXT.TEXTVALUE: We’ll require sodium sulphate, barium chloride, dil. HCl, a beaker, conical flask, test tubes, etc.
Take a small quantity of barium chloride in a test tube.
Transfer it into a conical flask.
Take a small quantity of sodium sulphate.
Transfer it into the conical flask containing barium chloride solution.
Stir the contents of the conical flask and keep it undisturbed for some time.
A white precipitate of barium sulphate is formed immediately. This confirms the presence of sulphate (SO[sub]4[/sub])[sup]2-[/sup] ions.
The precipitate of barium sulphate settles down to the bottom of the beaker.
Decant the upper solution from the conical flask into a beaker.
Then add a small quantity of dil. HCl into the conical flask containing the precipitate.
Then add a small quantity of dil. HCl into the conical flask containing the precipitate.
The white precipitate is insoluble in dil. HCl.
In this chemical reaction, sulphate ions are displaced by chloride ions and chloride ions are displaced by sulphate ions.This is a double displacement reaction.
